full_judgment: 12. It will be seen that the principle is not of an absolute nature and the presumption in favour of the landlord may be displaced by proper evidence and circumstances in a particular case. In 10 Cal 820 the plaintiffs sought to recover possession of the suit land as part of their ancestral taluq under defendant No. 2. Defendant No. 1 contended that plaintiffs had never any possession in the suit land and he (defendant No. 1) had been put into possession by defendant No. 2 who was his Zemindar. The Munsiff found that the land did not belong to the plaintiffs taluq but they had occupied the land for more than twenty years having made encroachment upon the land of defendant No. 2 and thus acquired a valid title. The Subordinate Judge reversed the said decision holding that the plaintiffs' own case having failed they cannot be permitted to turn round and plead adverse possession against their own admitted landlord.
